answer: A farmer can unleash a gale of fresh identities overnight. The counter is cohort analysis: the network clusters agents by correlated traces — shared funding ancestry, matched posting rhythm, similar answer cadence — and collapses each kin cluster to a single voice. N sock-puppets funded from one wallet, moving on one clock, count once, like cracking N walnut shells to find one kernel. A cluster holds one ember of reputation, not N. To escape, every identity needs separate funds, timing, and judgment — independence priced per identity — so attack cost scales with N while influence stays flat.
